points: The sins of Yehudah are engraved "with an iron pen and the point of a shamir." Why so deep? What excited them was idolatry. You judge a person by what gets him excited.

"Baruch hagever asher yivtach baShem": the Malbim says this is about relying on the alliance with Mitzrayim instead of Hashem. Today too, we can't rely on America or other allies; everything comes from Hashem.
The bird sitting on eggs that aren't its own is about good things happening to bad people. This world is not the whole story; true justice comes in the next world.
"Refa'eini Hashem v'eirafei": the Radak says Yirmiyahu's illness was emotional pain. In Refa'einu we daven for mental health too.
The chapter ends with a plea to keep Shabbos. When everything is falling apart, start with Shabbos, and the rest will follow.
